Now perform the moves with a script (verbatim blocks).

Now the C# edits.

I've fixed both problems and the related styling defects; the update is in the tar.gz above (29 files, extract at the repo root, nothing to delete). I couldn't compile or run the C# tests because this sandbox can't reach the .NET SDK or nuget.org, so please run `scripts/test.sh` before deploying. The JavaScript tests pass (317), and I checked the CSS fixes in a headless browser that copies how Blazor scopes component styles.

**The 400s on extra tabs and your phone.** The server allowed only 8 live connections per network address. Your 50 tabs and your phone on the same Wi‑Fi all share one address, so from the 9th connection on the server refused the live connection with a 429. The browser then fell back to slower connection methods, which the server always answers with 400. Refreshing still showed current results because the page itself loads fine; only the live part (the spinning reels) never connected.
- **Connection methods:** the server now offers only WebSockets, so a refused tab no longer falls back and hits the 400s.
- **Limits:** the defaults are now 64 connections per address and 400 in total, and both can be changed with environment variables. A household or a mobile carrier often puts many people behind one address, so 8 was too low.
- **Message:** a tab that still can't connect now says live updates couldn't start and suggests closing some tabs and reloading, instead of a generic error.

**The hidden text under "Your press worked."** This was the bigger pattern you suspected. The site-wide stylesheet had styles for the Work pages under common names, and they leaked into other pages that used the same names:
- **Slots and latency counter:** the sprint progress-bar style cut "14642 successful presses from this browser." down to a hidden half line.
- **Latency leaderboards:** the Work board style laid out each leaderboard's heading, empty message and list side by side in a sideways-scrolling row.
- **Reading history:** the Work history style indented it, shrank it and greyed it out.
- **Postcards:** the "Details" section was squashed into one row by a Work card style.
- **Homes details editor:** the details editor got the Work editor's spacing, and any text box in it a code font.
- **Slot badges:** they had an extra border.
- **Status lines:** they disappeared whenever empty, so the layout jumped around them.
- **Wrong colour:** "Saved.", "Link added." and "Sending your postcard…" appeared in error red. Successes are now green and progress messages grey.

The Work-only styles now live in each Work page's own stylesheet. The shared stylesheet keeps only colours, basic element styles and helpers that several pages share on purpose. I recorded that rule in a new ADR (0016), updated ADRs 0011 and 0012 and the README configuration table, and added tests for the new code.

# myblazorplayground — session notes

## First delivery (2026-11-19)

Full tar.gz (358 files). Domain / Data (Npgsql + Dapper, own migration runner) / Web (Work, Nest=homes, Chaos=toys, Identity, Administration). Ports 8090/5433, compose project `myblazorplayground`, tunnel container `myblazorplayground-tunnel`. `/setup` needs the one-time code from the log.

## Second delivery (2026-11-19, myblazorplayground-update2.tar.gz, 84 files)

- Root cause of the dead site: the Containerfile restores with only the .csproj files, so the SDK inferred `RequiresAspNetWebAssets=false`, never restored `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Internal.Assets`, and `publish --no-restore` silently shipped without `_framework/blazor.web.js` (404 -> HTML -> nosniff block -> no interactivity, Open button disabled). Fix: `<RequiresAspNetWebAssets>true</RequiresAspNetWebAssets>` in the Web csproj plus a publish-time guard in the Containerfile. The inline-script CSP warning is Cloudflare's injected script; HTML now sends `Cache-Control: ... no-transform`.
- Optional TOTP two-step sign in (ADR 0014): Domain `Totp`, `Base32`, `RecoveryCodes`, `Graphics/QrCode` (own QR encoder, inline SVG); migration 0003; `TwoFactorStore`; `TwoFactorService`; `/account/sign-in/code`; admin reset.
- Toys persist to PostgreSQL (ADR 0015, supersedes 0008): migration 0004; stores in `Data/Toys`; generic `WriteBehindJournal<T>` + `IStateLoader` (Nest refactored onto them).
- Latency per-client 5-minute cooldown removed (gap between runs stays). Reply is `ok <id>`.
- Responsive: nav wraps into a grid on phones, header not sticky under 40rem, tabs wrap, admin/settings tables stack, `.field { align-content: start }` fixes the Name/Key misalignment.
- Deleted: `Infrastructure/KeyedCooldowns.cs`, `Nest/INestJournal.cs`, `tests/.../Chaos/ClockAndCooldownTests.cs` (now `ClockTests.cs`).

Verified in the sandbox with real Npgsql 10 and Dapper built from source, a stub xunit runner, PostgreSQL 18 from conda-forge: domain 119 / web 371 / data 21, Vitest 311, Playwright TOTP end-to-end and 375px layout checks. Not verifiable here: blazor.web.js itself (the Internal.Assets package needs nuget.org).

## Third delivery (2026-11-24, myblazorplayground-update.tar.gz, 29 files, no deletions)

- Extra tabs / phone got `400` on `/_blazor?id=…`: `HubGuard` refused the WebSocket with 429 once an address held `MaxConnectionsPerClient` (8) connections; SignalR then fell back to SSE/long polling, which the guard answers with 400. Fix: `HubGuard.ConfigureConnection` (Transports = WebSockets) wired through `ServerComponentsEndpointOptions.ConfigureConnection` (exists since 11 preview 1); defaults 64 per client / 400 total; `#blazor-error-ui` is `data-permanent` and shows a "live updates could not start" message until a circuit opens (`trackCircuit` circuit handler in App.razor.js).
- Hidden slots/latency counter: global Work `.progress` (0.5rem, overflow hidden) leaked into the islands' `<p class="progress">`. Work-only global styles moved to isolated CSS (ADR 0016): BoardView, SprintsPage, ItemPage, RichEditor, WorkHome, Backlog. Also fixed: latency leaderboards laid out sideways (`.board`), reading history shrunk/indented (`.history`), postcard `.card .meta` as flex, listing `.editor` as grid with mono textarea, slot `.badge` border, island `.status` hidden when empty (layout jumps), success messages shown in red (new `wwwroot/js/status.js`, `data-tone="ok|note"`).
- Sandbox had no .NET SDK or nuget.org access this time: C# changes are unbuilt; Vitest 317 passing; CSS verified with a Playwright harness that emulates Blazor CSS scoping.
